E069-01.notes: Plural pronoun 'they' (the structures), past context 'Built in the 1920s and 1930s' -> 'were'. A/B singular with plural subject; D singular and present tense.

E069-02.notes: 'knots' is countable -> 'fewer knots'. A 'less' is for mass nouns; C 'a lesser amount of' same error, wordy; D 'a fewer number of' is ungrammatical (would be 'a smaller number of').

flags.note: 'A group of shop owners were worried' is accepted under notional agreement in many usage guides; ACT convention keys the singular head noun 'group', so D is the intended single best answer, but a well-read taker could hesitate.

E069-03.notes: Head noun 'group' is singular; past narrative -> 'was'. A/B plural ('have been' also wrong tense); C plural and present progressive, wrong tense.

E069-04.notes: Object of 'thanked' in compound 'Delia and ___' needs objective case 'me'. A/C/D are subject-case forms ('I', 'I myself', 'we'); D also changes meaning.

E069-05.notes: Possessive determiner needed: 'its cargo'. A/B = 'it is cargo', nonsense; D 'the ships cargo' lacks apostrophe (and plural would mismatch 'A ship').

E069-06.notes: 'existed before his' already conveys priority, so 'earlier' is redundant. A redundant (earlier + before); B doubly redundant (earlier, previous, before); C 'from an earlier time' still redundant and wordy; D 'several other designs' concise and clear.

E069-07.notes: Subject is singular 'flood' (intervening 'of requests from bakers'); past narrative -> 'was'. A/C plural; D plural and present perfect clashes with 'had to expand'.

E069-08.notes: Gerund phrase 'manufacturing them' is singular; past context -> 'was'. A/D plural; B plural and present tense clashes with 'burned out'.

E069-09.notes: Possessive 'its pieces' (the version's). A/B = 'it is pieces'; C 'its'' is not a word.

E069-10.notes: Relative possessive needed: 'Kwolek, whose curiosity outweighed her doubts, asked'. A/C 'who is curiosity' nonsense; D 'her curiosity outweighed her doubts' inserts an independent clause between subject and verb, ungrammatical.

E069-11.notes: 'Neither' is singular; 'of these' requires plural noun 'attempts'; past context -> 'attempts was'. A plural verb; B 'these attempt' noun-number error; D plural and present tense.

E069-12.notes: Singular 'Recognition', past narrative -> 'was'. A/B plural; C plural and present.

E069-13.notes: B: 'Weddell Sea, where it lay remarkably well preserved' - clean relative clause. A semicolon followed by fragment 'remarkably well preserved'; C comma splice; D colon followed by verbless 'it remarkably well preserved'.

E069-14.notes: Simple past matches narrative (1935-1943, 'grew'). A present perfect clashes with 'grew'; B future; D 'must have dismount' ungrammatical.

E069-15.notes: Compound subject 'The explosion and the fires' -> plural; past -> 'were'. A/B singular (B also present progressive); C singular and 'held responsible' changes meaning.

E069-16.notes: Design-to-look-natural is covered in one paragraph (sentences 2-5); essay then shifts to Seneca Village and eminent domain. A false (no tree-by-tree detail); C false (sunken roads are one sentence); D false (sentence 4 says almost every hill and pond was designed).
